blocks.text: Pay lesson by lesson or for a block in advance, by card or bank transfer. We send a receipt either way.

blocks.title: What happens in a lesson
blocks.text: Each lesson starts with what we'll work on and ends with what to practise. The progress card shows every skill and how far along it is.

blocks.title: Practising together
blocks.text: Private practice between lessons helps more than anything else. gov.uk sets out who can supervise a learner and what insurance you need.

items: Moving off and stopping on quiet roads

gearbox.title: Automatic or manual
gearbox.intro: Both are taught here. The licence you get is the difference.

blocks.title: Automatic
blocks.text: No clutch and no gears, so most people learn faster. Pass in an automatic and you can only drive automatics.

blocks.title: Manual
blocks.text: A clutch and gears to learn as well. Pass in a manual and you can drive both.

blocks.title: Not sure?
blocks.text: Book one lesson of each. You'll know by the end of the second.

intensive.title: Intensive courses
intensive.intro: Thirty hours over one to two weeks, for when you need to drive soon.

blocks.title: Who it suits
blocks.text: People who've had some lessons already, or who learn best with a lot of driving close together. If you've never driven, start with a few weekly lessons first.

blocks.title: How the days run

articles.title: Mirror, signal, then what?
articles.intro: Why the mirror check before a signal is the fault we see most.
body: Most learners check their mirrors. The fault is checking them too late, after the signal, or not acting on what they saw.
The order is mirrors, signal, then position and speed. Practise saying it out loud on quiet roads until it's automatic.

articles.title: Test-day nerves
articles.intro: What we do in the hour before a test.
body: We drive for forty minutes before the test, on roads you know, then arrive at the centre with ten minutes to spare.
Nerves are normal. The examiner isn't trying to catch you out; they want to see safe, independent driving.

questions.q: What do I need before my first lesson?
questions.a: A provisional driving licence. Bring it to the first lesson and we'll check it.

questions.q: How many lessons will I need?
questions.a: The DVSA's average is about 45 hours of lessons and 22 hours of private practice. Some people need fewer, some more. We'll tell you honestly as you go.

questions.q: Do I have to pay for a block up front?
questions.a: No. Pay lesson by lesson, or for a block in advance if you want the saving.

questions.q: What if I need to cancel?
questions.a: Cancel 48 hours before and there's nothing to pay.

questions.q: Can you pick me up from school?
questions.a: Yes, from home, school, college or work in the areas we cover.

questions.q: Will you take me to my test?
questions.a: Yes, in the car you learned in. Book the test on gov.uk and tell us the date.
